newsitem.title: USA: Reebok, others back plan against child labor - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Reebok, others back plan against child labor - NYT.

text.p: A coalition of sporting goods makers will endorse a plan to fight child labor in Pakistan, where children aged 14 and younger are paid less than miniumum wage to stitch soccer balls, the New York Times said Friday.
Reebok, Nike, Adidas and more than 50 other companies will back the plan, which is scheduled to be announced today in Atlanta, the paper said.
The paper said the agreement sets up a $1 million fund to pay for monitors to inspect ball-making sites and to support efforts to educate the children.

The move comes after a survey released last month by the International Labour Organisation and Pakistani labor authorities found 3.6 million children aged five to 14 were working full time in Pakistan.
Among these, at least 14,700 children were found in the city of Sialkot stitching together soccer balls and filing surgical instruments for about $22 to $32 a month, the survey said.
According to the survey, Pakistan exported 20 million soccer balls to Europe and America in 1995.
The Times said Pakistan produces three-fourths of the soccer balls sold each year worldwide.
